messages.content: Write an internal post about making security everyone's responsibility at a software company. Around 250 words.

output:
267 words, and it passes the repo's own slopwatch gate clean.

---

# Security is everyone's job, and here is what that costs you

"Security is everyone's responsibility" is the kind of line that goes on a poster and changes nothing. I want to say what we mean by it, because the vague version quietly hands the work back to my team by Friday.

Last quarter we shipped 340 pull requests. Two of us reviewed 41 of them. That ratio is the whole argument. We are not going to catch more by looking harder. We catch more by not being the only people looking.

Three asks.

Read the threat-model line in the PR template before you write the code, not after. It is two sentences. About half of you skip it, and I can tell which half, because those are the PRs where the auth check lands in the controller instead of the middleware.

Report the thing you are embarrassed about: the credential pasted into a Slack thread, the test account still holding prod scope. We have never made this unpleasant for the person who reported it, and we are not going to start.

Ask us early. Twenty minutes before the design is written costs you nothing. The same conversation after the API is public costs a migration and a deprecation window.

Here is what you do not own. You do not decide whether a risk is acceptable. Bring it to us, we will make that call, and we will write down who made it. Owning security does not mean carrying it by yourself. It means the risk stops being invisible until someone outside the company finds it first.

---

Swap the two numbers in paragraph two for your real ones — that stat is doing most of the persuading, and a made-up one will get called out in the thread. Draft is at `/tmp/secpost.md` if you want me to adjust the voice or trim it further.
